chunks: “The one emancipated by tadbīr is from the one-third. And whatever offense he commits, he, the mukātab, and the umm al-walad, then the master is liable for their offense.”

key_terms.أُمُّ الْوَلَدِ: A bondwoman who bore her master a child
key_terms.الثُّلُثِ: One-third of the estate or disposable portion in this legal context
key_terms.الْمَوْلَى: The master who bears legal responsibility here
key_terms.الْمُكَاتَبُ: A slave under a contractual arrangement for emancipation
key_terms.اَلْمُعْتَقُ عَنْ دُبُرٍ: A slave whose emancipation is made effective after the master's death
key_terms.لِجِنَايَتِهِمْ: For their offense or injury, meaning legal liability for what they commit

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a mudabbar’s status in the estate, and who bears liability for the offenses of a mudabbar, mukatab, and umm al-walad?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling on categories of enslaved persons in the law of emancipation and estate disposition. It explains that the mudabbar is counted within one-third of the estate, and that liability for offenses committed by the mudabbar, the mukatab, and the umm al-walad remains upon the master.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3468 - Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said:

"A mudabbar (a slave promised freedom after the owner's death) is counted as part of the one-third (of the estate). As for any offense committed by the mudabbar, the mukatab (a slave under a contract of emancipation), or the umm al-walad (a bondwoman who bore her master a child), the master is liable for their offenses."
